WAAREEENER.why: Large order book (about ₹47,000 crore, mostly with advances received) and capacity growth: it calls itself the largest non-Chinese solar module maker with 12 GW installed, and is adding US capacity (Texas plant). Q4 FY26 revenue more than doubled to ₹8,480 crore with profit up about 71%, though another report said the shares fell about 10.6% on a Q4 margin contraction.
WAAREEENER.outlook: Main overhang is US trade risk: a US customs finding that it evaded tariffs on cells from Vietnam and Malaysia cut the shares about 5% in a session and a broker flagged 65-70% of the order book as exposed to reputational issues. Motilal Oswal is Buy and JM Financial Add. Watch the US customs outcome, the India-US trade framework and the Q1 FY27 margin trend.

SAGILITY.why: Healthcare outsourcing demand: Q4 FY26 consolidated profit rose 43% and revenue about 29% to ₹2,024 crore, with 95% client retention, 17 new clients in FY26 and debt reduction helping profit. Nomura initiated at Buy (₹55 target) in March 2026 and the shares jumped 9%; Jefferies also raised its target in June.
SAGILITY.outlook: Management raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 21% with 25% adjusted EBITDA and reiterated low-double-digit growth for FY27. Nomura expects dollar revenue and rupee EPS to grow 12% and 20% over FY26-28 and argues AI handles simple queries while complex claims still need people. Not covered in sources: client concentration, US reimbursement policy and valuation after the rally.

SWIGGY.why: Below the IPO price because of quick-commerce losses. Q3 FY26 loss widened 33% to ₹1,065 crore (shares fell as much as 8%); Instamart's order value doubled to ₹7,938 crore but its loss was ₹908 crore. Q1 FY27 loss narrowed 34% to ₹791 crore on 37% revenue growth, yet shares fell 5% on 31 July as spending stayed high. Instamart reached contribution break-even in May 2026 but remains loss-making at adjusted EBITDA (₹778 crore loss in Q1).
SWIGGY.outlook: Food delivery is profitable (adjusted EBITDA margin 0.7% in Q3 FY26). Nomura is Buy at ₹435 and expects Instamart adjusted EBITDA losses of ₹3,100 crore in FY27 and ₹2,300 crore in FY28, funded by food delivery. CLSA is Hold and Macquarie Underperform. Management says it is past the March 2025 peak of losses but will keep investing against heavy competition.

BLACKBUCK.why: Revenue grew about 51-53% in FY26 and the shares more than doubled the IPO price, but they have moved sideways over the past year (about +3%; 52-week range ₹495-747). The company turned profitable, although sources disagreed on FY26 profit (one shows ₹164 crore, another a loss of ₹38 crore), so check the filing.
BLACKBUCK.outlook: Seven analysts averaged a Strong Buy with a mean target near ₹715, and revenue is forecast to grow 27% this year and 29% next. Simply Wall St sees earnings growing only 1.8% a year against 33.5% for revenue, so the market may doubt earnings quality or valuation. No specific 2026 catalyst was found.

MOBIKWIK.why: Fell on losses through 2025 (Q2 FY26 loss of about ₹28.6 crore, including a ₹11.8 crore charge for a fraudulent merchant settlement scheme) and was down about 52% over a year at one point, hitting a low near ₹151 on 30 March 2026. It then swung to a profit of ₹7.6 crore in Q1 FY27 (loss of ₹41.9 crore a year earlier) on operating leverage and lower lending costs, but revenue grew only 3.7%.
MOBIKWIK.outlook: Management gave FY27 profit and EBITDA guidance and changed how it will use IPO proceeds, shifting toward lending and payments. Risks: aggressive lending expansion strains cash flow, and payments face take-rate pressure. The shares did not hold the post-results rise.

IKS.why: Rebounded from a low near ₹1,262 to about ₹1,767 (5 October 2026) on steady margins and AI product momentum, including the Scribble Select ambient AI scribe launched in FY26. Its Aquity acquisition (October 2023) widened it into clinical documentation and coding for US healthcare clients. No single article explained the moves.
IKS.outlook: Investing.com consensus was Strong Buy with an average target near ₹1,898; ICICI Securities Buy at ₹2,080 but Nomura downgraded to Hold (₹1,640) in May 2026. P/E is about 49 against an industry figure near 14, so expectations are high; results depend on US healthcare clients.

HEXT.why: Below the IPO price after a guidance revision and repeated target cuts (one tracker cut its target from ₹801 to ₹554 in July, another to ₹440). It trades near ₹550 against a 52-week high of ₹900. Offsetting that: AI-led deal wins, an AI Ops platform launch (shares +7%) and being named an Anthropic authorised reseller for Amazon Bedrock. Q1 CY26 net profit rose 7.5% and revenue 12.6%.
HEXT.outlook: Management targets $3 billion revenue by 2029 (from about $1.5 billion), driven by AI, expansion and acquisitions. CEO Srikrishna Ramakarthikeyan steps down on 28 October 2026, a near-term uncertainty. The details of the guidance cut were not found.

ARISINFRA.why: Weak from the start: listed at ₹205 against a ₹222 issue price, then sold off through 2025-26 (about ₹110 in July 2026, against a 52-week high near ₹209). Earnings improved: FY26 revenue rose 39% to ₹1,067 crore and profit rose tenfold to ₹60.3 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% and profit nearly fourfold. So the fall looks like valuation and sentiment, not collapsing results.
ARISINFRA.outlook: Growth comes from contract manufacturing and its developer-as-a-service business; net debt-to-equity turned net cash (-0.09x). It won a ₹79 crore tunnel-project order in July 2026. Risks: steel and cement price swings, delays at contractor sites. Analyst coverage is thin (one analyst).

EBGNG.why: FY26 consolidated profit rose 91% to ₹132 crore with EBITDA up 59% and margin from 8.9% to 10.6%. India's largest laptop and desktop refurbisher benefits from higher average selling prices and widening affordability gaps as memory shortages and AI-led computing raise new-PC prices. The shares rose about 90% in six months from lows near ₹239; a director bought 1.35 lakh shares in June 2026.
EBGNG.outlook: Motilal Oswal is Buy with a ₹700 target (July 2026). Management guided a 22% rise in sales volume with only 3% price growth, read as a push for share over margin. Margins depend on raw-material (device) costs in a volatile hardware market.
